name: comparator-offset-mc
description: Monte-Carlo input-referred offset of the comparator front end over PVT, plus the part of that offset that moves across a +/-50 mV input-common-mode band.
claim: PLACEHOLDER DUT. sim/dut.json binds sim/dut/placeholder_comparator.spice (id placeholder-v1, provenance placeholder). This record substantiates the harness -- that a Monte-Carlo offset sweep over the mos_mismatch corner set genuinely runs and genuinely detects SG13G2's per-instance local mismatch -- and is NOT evidence toward README.md#target-specification's Offset-sigma row until design/comparator.sch exists and sim/dut.json is repointed at it (spec/porting-plan.md next step 1).

sig_vos_mv.description: MISMATCH-ON GUARD, not a spec bound. SG13G2's mismatch corner set (mos_*_mismatch) is what turns local mismatch on here -- there is no separate switch to forget. A deck that failed to select the mismatch corner (e.g. sabotaged to plain mos_tt) would report ~0 here while every other number in the record still looked plausible. 0.05 mV is far below anything a real sub-micron input pair can achieve, so this floor cannot be read as a design assertion -- it only catches a collapsed (mismatch-free) population. THIS IS ALSO THE HARNESS'S SABOTAGE NEGATIVE CONTROL FOR THIS BENCH: --sabotage-corners forces every corner to plain mos_tt (mismatch off, see sim/harness/corners.py), which must and does collapse this measurement toward exactly zero. The SPEC bound (README.md's Offset-sigma row) is deliberately NOT encoded as a check while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder: a placeholder passing or failing a spec row would be meaningless either way.

av_sigma_pct.description: LOAD-BEARING SELF-CHECK, not a design number. Each draw's gain is taken as (DC point at +2 mV minus DC point at 0 mV) within ONE `dc` sweep, which is only valid if the Monte-Carlo draw is constant across that sweep. If the draw were re-rolled per sweep point, (dv1 - dv0) would be dominated by the difference of two independent offsets rather than by the 2 mV probe, and the extracted gain would scatter by tens of percent. A few percent here is the proof that the draw was preserved, and therefore that every V_os in this record is a real offset rather than a difference of two populations.

mean_vos_sem.description: SYMMETRY CHECK, expressed in standard errors of the mean so it is independent of whatever sigma the bound DUT happens to have. The population mean offset must be ~0 because the circuit is nominally symmetric; +/-5 standard errors is a ~6e-7 two-sided false-alarm rate at this N. A mean outside it means a systematic asymmetry is riding on top of the mismatch -- a netlist error, or a genuinely asymmetric topology.

vbias_anchor_mv.description: CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR. The bias pin's own voltage is a V_th proxy and is strongly corner- and temperature-dependent, unlike the mismatch sigma above, which is corner-invariant almost by construction (the agauss() mismatch terms live in the LV MOS subckt, not in any corner section's typical/skew parameters). Without an anchor this manifest would have very little that could fail under --sabotage-corners on the process/temperature axes specifically (sig_vos_mv already catches sabotage via the mismatch-on guard above, but that is a mismatch check, not a process-corner-sensitivity one). Deliberately measured on `ibn`, a CONTRACT node (the DUT's ibias pin), not an internal node, so it survives a DUT swap. Floors calibrated from this experiment's first committed 45-point record (named in this experiment's README.md, run --no-write during issue #8 development), with ~55% margin below the observed weakest slices (process 25.08%, temperature 26.83%). The supply axis is deliberately unfloored: a diode-connected mirror's gate voltage is set by the forced bias current and is essentially supply-independent by design (observed weakest supply slice: 0.17%), so a floor there would fail for a correct circuit.

evidence.mc_seed: ngspice `set rndseed=20260910` at the top of the control block, then 200 draws per PVT point via `reset` inside a `dowhile` loop (each reset re-evaluates the agauss() expressions the PDK's sg13_lv_nmos/sg13_lv_pmos subckts carry -- confirmed against the installed checkout during issue #6, sim/device-mismatch-confirm/README.md). The SAME seed is used at every PVT point -- common random numbers -- so movement of the reported sigma across the grid is a real PVT effect and not sampling noise; N for statistical-error purposes is 200, not 200 x 45.
evidence.mc_scope: mismatch-only. The mos_mismatch corner set (mos_{tt,ff,ss,fs,sf}_mismatch) is both the process-corner axis AND the Monte-Carlo mismatch switch at once -- see sim/harness/corners.py's module docstring for why SG13G2 has no equivalent of a separable global mismatch switch. Global process skew is swept deterministically by the corner axis itself (tt/ff/ss/fs/sf), so the two are never confounded in one number.
evidence.mc_sigma: 1-sigma of the input-referred offset is reported directly, alongside the 3-sigma value a comparator offset spec is conventionally stated at. Statistical precision on each sigma is 1/sqrt(2N) = 5.0% at N = 200. Offset per draw is -dv(0 mV)/A_v where A_v is measured on the SAME draw from the 0 mV and +2 mV points of one `dc` sweep; av_sigma_pct is the check that the draw really was preserved between them.
notes: TWO DC POINTS PER DRAW, ONE INSTANCE. Gain is measured inside a single `dc` sweep of the shared differential source, not from a second instance. Two instances would have independent mismatch draws, so their difference would contain an offset difference rather than just the gain.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS RECORD. (a) The decision stage's own offset -- it has no DC operating point, so this method cannot reach it at all. (b) Load-resistor mismatch -- this placeholder's front-end load is an ideal SPICE resistor, not a PDK resistor subckt, so there is no resistor mismatch term to include or null-control (see sim/dut/placeholder_comparator.spice's header). (c) Any layout-induced systematic offset -- this is a schematic-level (in fact placeholder-level) record.

THE COMMON-MODE BAND IS +/-50 mV ABOUT dut_vcm AND IT IS A STANDALONE CHOICE. There is no CDAC or SAR sequencer here to inherit a band from; the band is a stated property of the comparator's own input range.

EVERY sqrt() IN THIS BLOCK IS GUARDED WITH abs() (issue #8). A variance term (e.g. svaq/nmax - (sva/nmax)^2) that is mathematically ~0 -- which happens whenever the underlying corner carries no mismatch, e.g. a plain (non-`_mismatch`) `mos_*` corner such as `--corners tt`, or `--sabotage-corners` forcing every corner to `mos_tt` -- can land a few ULPs on the negative side of zero from floating-point summation order. ngspice's sqrt() of a negative real returns a COMPLEX result, printed as `real,imag` (e.g. `0.0000000000e+00,8.0920713114e-14`), which does not match this harness's `m_<name> = <float>` measurement regex at all -- the point then fails as 'no measurements parsed' instead of cleanly reporting sig_vos_mv ~ 0 mV and failing the mismatch-on guard above for the intended reason. sqrt(abs(...)) makes the mismatch-off case report a clean near-zero sigma (still correctly failing the >= 0.05 mV floor) instead of a parse failure. Confirmed empirically during issue #8: sim/characterize.sh smoke uses `--corners tt_mismatch` (not plain `tt`) for this experiment specifically so its 200-draw loop always has real mismatch to measure; `--sabotage-corners` still collapses every corner to plain `mos_tt`, so the guarded formulas are what make its FAIL land on the documented mismatch-on-guard check rather than on a parse error.
